rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose adjective for an unusually imaginative or unrealistic idea.

example.english: Your idea is really fanciful—how could a house possibly be built within a month?
example.traditional: 你呢個諗法真係異想天開，點可能一個月內起好間屋呀？
example.jyutping: nei5 ne1 go3 nam2 faat3 zan1 hai6 ji6 soeng2 tin1 hoi1 dim2 ho2 nang4 jat1 go3 jyut6 noi6 hei2 hou2 gaan1 uk1 aa3

rows.note: Use this when the imagination or ideas range freely, especially in writing or creative work.

example.english: The plots in their novels are always fanciful; they can write anything.
example.traditional: 佢啲小說情節一向天馬行空，乜嘢都寫得出。
example.jyutping: keoi5 di1 siu2 syut3 cing4 zit3 jat1 hoeng3 tin1 maa5 hang4 hung1 mat1 je5 dou1 se2 dak1 ceot1

rows.note: Use this when the emphasis is that the fanciful idea is impractical or detached from real-world constraints.

example.english: The idea that one person can handle the whole project is really fanciful.
example.traditional: 話一個人做晒成個項目，真係不切實際。
example.jyutping: waa6 jat1 go3 jan4 zou6 saai3 seng4 go3 hong6 muk6 zan1 hai6 bat1 cit3 sat6 zai3
